messages:
anya: quick heads-up — noticed chat template + tokenizer combo inserting an extra BOS token when serving the new weights from s3. example repro below, looks like a formatting delta vs the repo tokenizer. :confused:

sam: can you paste the prompt + tokenized output? want to check if it's a template issue or tokenization mapping. :eyes:

anya: yup. minimal repro (ran on my laptop against the tokenizer files from the onboarding bundle):

anya: ```
# template used by service
chat = [ {role: 'system', content: 'You are a helpful assistant.'}, {role: 'user', content: 'Hello'} ]
# tokenizer output (ids)
>> [101, 1, 102, 500, 2]
# expected pattern: [BOS, <role_delim>, ... , EOS] but we get an extra 1 before the user content
```

tariq: which model dir / tokenizer files did you pull? path?

anya: s3://redwood-models/onboard/llama3c-v2/weights/ and tokenizer at s3://redwood-models/onboard/llama3c-v2/tokenizer/ (same bundle used in PR). config.yaml has chat_template: "<|bos|><role><|sep|>{content}<|eos|>"

sam: can you run the tokenizer check script? infra has `tokenizer_check.py` that validates special tokens + template substitution. cmd: `python infra/tools/tokenizer_check.py --model-dir s3://... --template-file ./config.yaml`

anya: ran it, output: 

anya: ```
[INFO] loading tokenizer from s3://redwood-models/onboard/llama3c-v2/tokenizer/
[WARN] unknown special token placeholder: <|role|> -> falling back to whitespace
[ERR] detected duplicate BOS token insertion for chat template at positions [0,2]
[FAIL] template validation: mismatched token boundaries
```

tariq: hmm. looks like the tokenizer mapping doesn't have the custom `<|role|>` placeholder -> template engine substitutes an empty token which then shifts token offsets and triggers double BOS. That matches my prior bug with the llama3 checkpoints where role_delim changed.

sam: is this specific to the hosted serving runtime or also happens with local tokenization?

anya: reproduces locally against the shipped tokenizer files. Hosted runtime also sees it (observed in a canary run — logs attached).

sam: thanks. triage plan: 1) add a quick unit test to infra/tools to assert that all placeholders in config.yaml map to actual special tokens in tokenizer vocab, 2) update the onboarding checklist to include `tokenizer_check.py` run, 3) patch tokenizer mapping in the model bundle if needed.

tariq: I'll own the unit test + CI check. will open PR against infra with a test that loads s3 bundle and fails if placeholders unresolved. assigning to @sam for review.

sam: thanks. can you also add a quick note in the model onboarding doc about verifying role delimiter token ids? short blurb under "tokenizer quirks".

anya: created a tiny gist showing the offending mapping and suggested fix (replace `<|role|>` with `<|sep|>` in config for this model). gist: https://gist.github.com/anya/abcd1234

tariq: PR #3821 opened — adds test + small validator. CI currently running. linking artifacts: https://ci.redwood.dev/3821

ci-bot: PR 3821: CI started. unit tests: tokenizer_check_test.py -> running. :robot_face:

sam: once CI green, we'll patch the model bundle and re-run the canary. after that, rollback plan: if canary latency/regression shows token misalignment, fallback to previous model variant (dedicated: model:v1.2).

anya: noted. I'm going to run a quick sanity pass on the live canary and post logs after.

tariq: ETA for PR review is end of day. I'll ping infra oncall if CI flakes.

anya: thanks all. small follow-up: we should add a short entry in eng-ml runbook about this class of BOS/EOS/template mismatch — saved us a few hours. :+1:

sam: agreed — adding to backlog as task INFRA-2145.

ci-bot: PR 3821: all checks passed. :white_check_mark:
